To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed the WebFlow metacomputing programming environment for high performance web-based metacomputing and demonstrated that the environment can be used to solve real-world problems in computational science and engineering.

(a) WebFlow is a prototype for the new generation of metacomputing programming tools, which is based on the new software infrastructure of the web, and (b) WebFlow is the first metacomputing tool to use the new Globus metacomputation toolkit as the backend for its middle-tier.
the web is a powerful platform for building metacomputing systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the next generation HPCC programming environment that is based on web technologies and metacomputing.

the development of a new class of high-performance, high-functionality programming tools for metacomputing and grid computing that are sustainable in that they can be built on top of the commercial web infrastructure and thus will not be obsolete when the next generation of commercial web infrastructure arrives.
the development of the new HPCC programming environment that is based on the Globus Toolkit and the Java programming language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the web is the new metacomputing environment.
WebFlow is a fully functional and robust prototype for a new generation of HPCC programming tools.
WebFlow is a new programming paradigm for metacomputing that provides a high level of abstraction and ease of use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully demonstrated a prototype of a Web-based metacomputing programming environment.
we are able to use commodity hardware and software to provide the same level of functionality that is available on the high end systems, and at a fraction of the cost.
the Web is the future for HPCC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to create a highly sophisticated, robust, and easy-to-use metacomputing environment on the basis of the new web infrastructure.
the HPCC programming model and the web programming model can co-exist in a single environment.
HPCC is not a new computing paradigm but rather a way to use existing technologies in new ways.
